pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on September 15, 2026, the U.S. Census Bureau released its official income and poverty estimates for 2025 from the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement. Real median household income was $87,460 in 2025, an increase of 2.6% from $85,210 in 2024 after adjusting for inflation, and the highest on record in data going back to 1967. Median post-tax household income rose 3.1%. The official poverty rate fell 0.5 percentage points to 10.2%, and the official child poverty rate fell to a historic low of 13.4%. Household income at the 10th percentile and the Supplemental Poverty Measure rate (13.1%) did not change significantly, and median earnings of men working full time, year round did not change significantly while women's rose 3.2%.
